newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy deputy pm criticises Chirac on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy deputy pm criticises Chirac on EMU.

text.p: Italian deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni called on French President Jacques Chirac on Tuesday to withdraw remarks questioning Italy's ability to join Europe's single currency and accused him of meddling in Rome's affairs.
"If these statements by Chirac aren't denied, we cannot but view them as grave, grave because our country has made an exceptional effort to enter Europe," Veltroni told reporters.
"Chirac has every right to look at the state of his own country, without interfering in the internal choices of a country which is putting together a budget," Veltroni said.
"We don't pass judgment on what others do and we expect others to act the same way," he said.

Chirac, speaking earlier in northern France ahead of a planned Italian-Franco summit later this week, said Italy may not be among the first group of countries to join a single currency in 1999. He also said French exports had suffered from a devaluation of the Italian lira as well as the pound and peseta.
Italy's centre-left government last week unveiled a stringent 1997 budget which it says will put the country on track to meet the tough economic criteria required for membership.
